tools.name: get-function-count
tools.title: Get Function Count
tools.description: Get the total count of functions in the program (use this before calling get-functions to plan pagination)

programPath.description: Path in the Ghidra Project to the program to get functions from

filterDefaultNames.description: Whether to filter out default Ghidra generated names like FUN_, DAT_, etc.

tools.name: set-function-prototype
tools.title: Set Function Prototype
tools.description: Set or update a function prototype using C-style function signatures. Can create new functions or update existing ones.

programPath.description: Path in the Ghidra Project to the program

signature.description: C-style function signature (e.g., 'int main(int argc, char** argv)')

location.description: Address or symbol name where the function is located

createIfNotExists.description: Create function if it doesn't exist at the location

tools.name: get-decompilation
tools.title: Get Function Decompilation
tools.description: Get decompiled code for a function with line range support. Defaults to 50 lines to conserve context - start with small chunks (10-20 lines) then expand as needed using offset/limit. Updating variable data types and names can significantly improve decompilation quality. Use includeCallers/includeCallees to get caller/callee lists in one call (avoids separate tool invocations).

functionNameOrAddress.description: Function name, address, or symbol to decompile (e.g. 'main', '0x00401000', or 'start'). For addresses pointing inside a function, the containing function will be decompiled.

includeCallers.description: Include list of functions that call this one (name, address, signature). Use for understanding function usage without bulk decompilation.

programPath.description: Path in the Ghidra Project to the program containing the function

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-based). Defaults to 1.

includeDisassembly.description: Whether to include assembly listing alongside decompilation for sync

includeIncomingReferences.description: Whether to include incoming cross references to this function on the function declaration line

limit.description: Number of lines to return. Defaults to 50 lines to conserve context. Use smaller chunks (10-20 lines) for initial exploration, then expand as needed.

includeReferenceContext.description: Whether to include code context snippets from calling functions (requires includeIncomingReferences)

includeComments.description: Whether to include comments in the decompilation output

includeCallees.description: Include list of functions this one calls (name, address, signature). Use for understanding function dependencies without bulk decompilation.

signatureOnly.description: Return only signature/metadata without decompiled code. Saves output tokens.

tools.name: find-cross-references
tools.title: Find Cross References
tools.description: Find all references to or from a memory location, symbol, or function. Returns incoming and/or outgoing references with optional decompilation context.

includeContext.description: Include decompilation context snippets for code references

contextLines.description: Number of lines before and after to include in context snippets

programPath.description: Path in the Ghidra Project to the program to get references from

limit.description: Maximum number of references to return per direction

location.description: Address or symbol name to get references for (e.g., '0x00400123', 'main', 'FUN_00401000')

direction.description: Direction of references to retrieve: 'to' (incoming), 'from' (outgoing), or 'both' (default)

tools.name: get-data-type-by-string
tools.title: Get Data Type by String
tools.description: Get a data type by its string representation

programPath.description: Path in the Ghidra Project to the program

dataTypeString.description: String representation of the data type (e.g., 'char**', 'int[10]')

archiveName.description: Optional name of the data type archive to search in. If not provided, all archives will be searched.

tools.name: run-script
tools.title: Run Python Script
tools.description: Execute a Python script in the Ghidra PyGhidra runtime against a specific program. Requires Ghidra to be launched via PyGhidra (mcp-reva or pyghidra-gui). Returns captured stdout/stderr, duration, and timeout flag. Script failures appear in stderr with success=false; tool failures (bad args, PyGhidra unavailable) are MCP errors. Cancellation is cooperative: long-running scripts should periodically check monitor.isCancelled() so the timeout can fire on tight loops.

scriptPath.description: Absolute path to an existing .py script to run.

programPath.description: Path to the program in the Ghidra Project

code.description: Inline Python source. The script runs as a Ghidra script with currentProgram, FlatProgramAPI helpers, and monitor available. Wrap state changes in currentProgram.startTransaction(...) / endTransaction(...) yourself — the tool does not open a transaction. Provide exactly one of: code, scriptPath, scriptName.

scriptName.description: Name of a script (e.g., 'MyAnalysis.py') resolved across registered Ghidra script directories.

timeoutSeconds.description: Per-call timeout override in seconds. Defaults to the configured script timeout.

tools.name: list-scripts
tools.title: List Scripts
tools.description: List Python scripts visible to Ghidra across all registered script directories (user dir + system dirs + bundle dirs). Filterable by path or name; supports pagination.

pathFilter.description: Optional substring filter on script absolute path

nameFilter.description: Optional substring filter on script file name

tools.name: read-script
tools.title: Read Script
tools.description: Read a script's source, returned with cat -n style line numbers so you can reference exact lines in edit-script. Supports chunked reads via offset/limit. Sets truncated=true if more lines remain.

scriptPath.description: Absolute path to the script. Provide either scriptPath or scriptName.

scriptName.description: Script file name resolved across registered script directories.

tools.name: write-script
tools.title: Write Script
tools.description: Create a new script or fully replace an existing one in a writeable script directory. System directories are read-only. Use edit-script for targeted changes instead of full rewrites.

scriptPath.description: Absolute path; must resolve under a writeable script directory.

scriptName.description: File name (e.g., 'MyAnalysis.py') — written to the default writeable scripts directory.

overwrite.description: Overwrite existing file. Default false: errors if file exists.

tools.name: edit-script
tools.title: Edit Script
tools.description: Replace exact old_string with new_string in a script. Errors if old_string isn't found, or if it matches multiple locations and replace_all is false. Use this instead of write-script when iterating on an existing script.

scriptPath.description: Absolute path to the script to edit (must be writeable).

old_string.description: Exact text to find. Must occur exactly once unless replace_all is true; surround with enough context to make it unique.

scriptName.description: Script file name resolved under the default writeable scripts directory.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence. Default false: errors if old_string matches more than one location.

new_string.description: Replacement text. Must differ from old_string.
